title: What has changed in the Colorway Editor in CLO 7.3?
content: ### **Question** What has changed in the Colorway Editor in CLO 7.3? ### **Answer** In CLO 7.3, creating colorways has become more diverse and easier compared to previous versions. You can now create colorways with increased variety, similar to actual colorways. The specific changes include: The number of each item can increase as much as the number of colorways, and by default, only the selected items are displayed in the Object Browser. **ℹ️Note** : Check out the entire colorway workflow in the [manual](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000563748-Colorway) or on [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WRkb4MR0dP0&t=3837s). **1️⃣ Create more colorways by adding various items with different properties such as texture, buttons, topstitching, etc.** In previous versions, adding items with different properties was not possible, limited to changing textures and colors only. However, starting from CLO 7.3, properties like texture, types, and sizes of buttons can be edited. ![Frame 238.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/25551707984665) ** 2️⃣ Manage identical items across different colorways ** When using certain items with the same properties across multiple colorways, you can now change all properties across those colorways by modifying just one item. **3️⃣****When applying each item (Fabric, Graphics, Buttons, Buttonholes, Topstitching, Puckering, Accessories) to a pattern, you can choose how they will be applied to the colorway.******* Latest Updated on February 22, 2024, ver 7.3.240.46861 See the examples below and make your own selections as needed. You can learn how to apply each item [here](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002273487--Object-Browser-Apply-Button-Style). ![Assign to Pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/30073324508825) **A. Assign to the current colorway only** This option is used when you want to apply different variations to selected colorway only. ![Frame 287.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/30073324557593) **B. Assign to all colorways by linking color chips to change simultaneously** Apply to all colorways, but if the fabric is the same for each colorway, selecting a color chip will automatically select the same fabric across colorways. ![Frame 288.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/30073324589209) **C. Assign to all colorways by unlinking color chips so they change separately** Apply to all colorways, but each colorway is a different fabric. ![Frame 289.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/30073706126361) ### **FAQ ** **Q1.****When I add a different item to existing colorways, I cannot seem to edit them individually. How can I solve this problem?** When adding a different item to existing colorways, they will be added with the same properties. If you wish to change properties in individual colorways, right-click on the color chip, then select 'Unlink All Colorways' to make individual edits. **Q2.****When I save a colorway file from the updated version and open it in a lower version, the colorway information disappears. How can I solve this issue?** The new colorway format is not compatible with lower versions. As the colorway feature will be updated continuously, we recommend using the latest version. **Q3. The****Colorway Editor seems to be slower than in previous versions. Why is that?** Each colorway consists of different items, which requires more time to update. However, we are continuously working on improving the speed issue, and incremental improvements will be made.
content_description: Discover the enhanced features of the Colorway Editor in CLO 7.3, designed to make creating diverse and customizable colorways easier than ever.

title: Module Structure
content: Module is a system that allows you to adjust the designs easily and combine them part by part. Please see the terminology for the Module below in order to have a better understanding in the Modular Mode. ![Modular_M.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026787527/Modular_M.jpg) **A: Module Structure:** A state when a Block Box that consists of a Garment is sewn to another. When sewing a Block Box that is in this Block Structure to a Pattern, it automatically creates Sewing Lines in between the Patterns as it is already interlocked. **B:** **Pattern:** Patterns to be included in a Block that will be adjusted partially. Patterns in the Modular Mode can be modified and sewn the same as the Simulation Mode. **C:** **Block Box:** A frame that consists of a Module Structure. **D:** **Block:** A state when Patterns are sewn to Block Boxes. Blocks that have the same Block Boxes can be replaced with each other.
content_description: Discover how to effortlessly customize and assemble designs using the Module system, which allows for seamless integration of various components in Modular Mode.

title: V-Ray Render Properties
content: **List of Contents** Render Properties Engine Noise Threshold Max, Render Time (min) **Render Properties YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gJ06vDjNg04 **\- Edit render properties applied to final render output. \- Select the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026324647/mceclip0.png) **Render Properties** tool from the Render toolbar and navigate to the Property Editor. ** Engine YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1RTPJI94pHc ** \- Decide the core engine used during render among CPU, GPU (CUDA,) and GPU (OpenCL). * **CPU** \- Use CPU when render. * **GPU(CUDA)** \- Use GPU (CUDA) when render. * **GPU(OpenCL)** \- Use GPU (OpenCL) when render. . \- The option does not appear in Mac. **Noise Threshold YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U7rXCIdUsPs ** \- Decide the amount of noise shows in the final render image. \- Default value is 0.01 and it can be adjusted between 0.001 and 0.015. \- Bigger the Noise Threshold is, more noise appears. **Max, Render Time (min) YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=howIckfKQOQ ** \- The rendering process only takes about two minutes on average when default settings are used for Light Properties, Image/Video Properties, and Render Properties. \- However, the render time may differ when properties are modified. To prevent extensive delay, limit the time used for rendering each image by configuring the **Max, Render Time (min)**. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides essential guidance on adjusting render properties, selecting rendering engines, managing noise thresholds, and optimizing render times for improved final output quality.

title: Troubleshooting AI Import Failures
content: **List of Contents** Case 1 (There are Pattern points that are too close together) Case 2 (Pattern outlines are intersecting) Case 3 (This is an unsupported file type.) **Objective** Learn how to fix AI import failures respective to the types of error messages. **Case 1** ![Case_1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115018795768/Case_1.png) **Cause of Error:** When the points on the patterns are too close to each other. **Solution A - Delete & Join Points in Adobe Illustrator** 1. Open the file with issue in the Adobe Illustrator. 2. Find points too closed to each other and delete one of them. → As the point is deleted, the line is disconnected. 3. Use the Average and Join function to reconnect the line. 4. Save the file again and open in CLO. → The pattern file opens properly in CLO. **Solution B - Adjust Pattern Size in CLO** 1. Navigate to the Main Menu and select File > Import > **Adobe (AI/PDF)**. → The Import AI/PDF window appears. 2. Deselect Auto Scale. 3. Increase the Scale percentage or select larger pattern unit and select OK. → The pattern file opens properly. **※ Note:** * If the pattern file still does not open properly, further increase the Scale percentage or select even larger pattern unit. Then, open the file again. * When the percentage and the unit is changed, the size of the pattern imported in CLO may differ from the original pattern size. **Case 2** ![Case_2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115018703567/Case_2.png) **Cause of Error:** When the lines on patterns are intersecting. **Solution** 1. Open the file with issue in Adobe Illustrator. 2. Find and edit the intersecting lines. 3. Save the file and re-open in CLO. → The file opens properly. **Case 3** ![Case_3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115018703587/Case_3.png) **Cause of Error A:** When the Create PDF Compatible File option is not checked when saving the file in Adobe Illustrator. **Solution** 1. Open the file with issue in Adobe Illustrator. 2. Navigate to the Main Menu > File > Save as... 3. Assign the saving path and the file name. Then, click Save. 4. Check Create PDF Compatible File and click OK. 5. Reopen the file in CLO. → The file opens properly. **Cause of Error B:** When a line of a pattern is disconnected. ** Solution ** 1. Open the file with issue in Adobe Illustrator. 2. Find the disconnected pattern outline. 3. Use the Average and Join function to reconnect the line. 4. Save the file again and open in CLO. → The pattern file opens properly in CLO. **※ Note: ** * For**Case 2** and **Case 3** , create a rectangle surrounding all patterns with issue, save in Adobe Illustrator, and then reopen in CLO as internal lines to open them without any pattern modification. * To use the Internal Lines as Patterns, use the [**Trace tool** ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000307728) or the [**Clone as Pattern** ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000343287)option to convert Internal Lines to Patterns. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides solutions for common AI import failures in CLO, detailing how to resolve issues related to closely spaced points, intersecting outlines, and unsupported file types.

title: Polygon Lasso Selection
content: ### **Objective** Select Patterns, Sewing Lines, Topstitches, and Puckering with more freedom. ### **Location** Main Menu ▶ Edit tool for the respective item 3D/ 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit tool for the respective item **※ Note: ** **Edit Tools for Respective Items** --- **Pattern** | ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054817674/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** (A) **Line/Point** | ![mceclip3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054817754/mceclip3.png) **Edit Pattern** (Z) **Sewing** | **![mceclip4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055698773/mceclip4.png)Edit Sewing** (B) **Topstitches** | **![mceclip5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054817794/mceclip5.png)Edit Topstitch** (J) **Puckering** | ![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054817814/mceclip6.png) **Edit Puckering** **Buttons/Buttonholes** | ![mceclip7.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055698873/mceclip7.png) **Select/Move Button** ([) **Seam Allowances** | ![seam_allowance.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026824807/seam_allowance.png) **Seam Allowance** **Grading** | ![grading.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026824827/grading.png) **Grading** **UV** | **![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054818354/mceclip0.png)Edit UV** ### ### **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Edit tool for the respective item 3D/ 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit tool for the respective item 2. Double click in the 2D window, then drag the mouse. → A selection point appears where the mouse is double clicked and a line follows as the mouse is dragged. 3. Click around the items to create the lasso selection. 4. Click on the start point to complete the lasso selection. → All items related to the Edit tool are selected and highlighted in yellow. **※ Note:** Only items related to the activated Edit tool are selected. For example, if the ![mceclip3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054817754/mceclip3.png) **Edit Pattern** tool is used to create a polygon lasso selection, only segments and points within the lasso selection are selected.
content_description: Explore the freedom to select and edit patterns, sewing lines, topstitches, and puckering with intuitive tools in our 3D/2D interface.

title: CLO Under System Maintenance
content: CLO system maintenance is carried out to provide a seamless service for all of our users. Usually the entire process takes on average an hour. **W hat will be affected by system maintenance?** During maintenance, the items listed below might be unavailable. * Access to CLO software * CLO installer downloads * Sign-up (Email verification) * Change password * Sending Invoice * Subscription related emails **Will I be notified when system maintenance is completed?** Once the system is back, the CLO website banner will be back to normal. If this turns into an extended outage, we will update the status on [CLO social media channels](https://discord.gg/phNYjpj5VX). Should you have additional inquiries (or if you have trouble accessing CLO software or the installer download page after the website banner is restored) please [contact us](https://clo3d.com/en/support/contactus). We apologize for any inconvenience caused, the CLO team is working to deliver a better user experience. CLO Support Team
content_description: This web page informs users about scheduled CLO system maintenance, its potential impacts, and provides updates and support resources to ensure a seamless user experience.

title: Fill (ver 6.2)
content: **List of Contents** Duplicate Property ### **Objective** Create a realistic puffy garment by setting the fill type and weight. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VuJyDM7hYHs **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ **Fill** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4409935066265/mceclip0.png) **Fill** **Operation** **Duplicate** 1. Click the tool/menu indicated.** ** 2. Click the piece to be applied or, Click anywhere in the 2D window ▶ Drag your cursor to select the pieces within the marquee. ** **→ The duplicated pieces appear on the mouse cursor. 3. Click the position where you place the duplicated piece. → The outlines of both pieces are sewn, and the internal lines crossed with them are sewn as well. → Display in purple. 4. Select any grey quilt lines to turn on the quilting effect. **Property** 1. Click the puffy pattern piece. **→** Filer Property appears in the Property Editor. 2. Once the puffy properties are set, simulate the garment.** ** **Property**** ** | **Description** ---|--- **Filer** | Type | Choose the type of filler. Weight | Enter the weight of the filler. **※Note:** Select multiple pattern pieces to set the total weight. The weight of each piece is calculated and distributed proportionally. Quilting Distance | Enter the quilting distance. ![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4409111186457/mceclip2.png) **※Note:** Fill Volume is calculated based on the Quilting Distance and the Weight. Quilting Distance indicates the distance between the internal lines used as quilting lines, and you must input the distance value. If the internal lines are neither parallel nor their distance is constant, please enter the widest value. → You can have a reasonably realistic puffiness based on the pressure set by the weight and the quilting volume. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating realistic puffy garments in Clo3D by utilizing fill properties and duplication techniques.

title: Create .HW File and Register .LCN File
content: **Operation** 1. Click on the circled area to fully display the Login window. ![lcnfile0-1.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115015151428) 2. Check or uncheck the circled areas according to the image below, then click on **Create HW File**. **※ Note:** When creating file, save the file name as your user ID. ![lcnfile1-1.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115015151448) 3. Send the newly created .HW file to [support@clo3d.com](mailto:support@clo3d.com%C2%A0and), for a .LCN file request. 4. Download the .LCN file received from the CLO Support Team. 5. Check or uncheck the circled areas according to the image below, then click on **Register LCN File**. ![lcnfile3.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115015151488) 6. Once the .LCN file is registered and below message appears, click **OK** to go back to the Login window. ![lcnfile2.JPG](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115015066907) 7. Double check on the check-boxes' status and the 'Registered' message with a check icon below the **Register LCN File** button, then click **Log In** to run the the program. ![lcnfile4-1.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115015151468)
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for creating and registering a .HW file to obtain a .LCN file for logging into the CLO software.

title: Edit Piping Length
content: ### Objective Edit the length of Piping. **Location** Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Piping ▶ **Edit Piping** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005677008/________.png) **Edit Piping** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Piping ▶**Edit Piping** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005677008/________.png)**Edit Piping** → An editable line appears on top of all Piping, and also a hidden Piping appears in semi-transparent temporarily. 2. title: [Property] Set Sublayer
content: ### **Objective** Assign orders to the Sewing Lines on a Pattern which folds on itself such as seam allowances and pleats in order to increase simulation stability. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **Edit Sewing** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001218987/________.png) **Edit Sewing** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **Edit Sewing** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001218987/________.png) **Edit Sewing** → All established Sewing Lines appear in the 2D window. 2. Select the Sewing Lines to set Sublayer. → Sewing Line properties appear in the property editor. 3. Toggle on the **Set Sublayer** option. → A red arrow which indicates the order of the selected pair of Sewing Lines appear. **※ Note:** The half of the seam next to the arrow head is fixed and the other half next to the arrow tail moves according to the setting. 4. Change the Sublayer setting as needed. **Reverse Direction** | Swap the fixed Sewing Line and the moving Sewing Line. ---|--- **Front** | **Back** | Decide which side of the fabric is attached to the fixed Sewing Line. 5. Activate **Simulation**. → Changes are applied respective to the setting.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for assigning orders to Sewing Lines in order to enhance simulation stability in pattern design.

title: [Popup] Activate/Deactivate Sewing Lines
content: ### **Objective** Activate or deactivate Sewing Lines as needed. Use this function when Sewing Lines should be applied after garment is draped such as the back slits for a men's jacket. ** Location ** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001223227/________.png) Edit Sewing ▶ Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) ▶ **Deactivate/Activate Sewing (Selected)** Object Browser ▶ Scene Tab ▶ Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Item) ▶ **Deactivate/Activate Sewing (Selected)** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001223227/________.png) Edit Sewing ▶ Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) ▶ **Deactivate/Activate Sewing (Selected)** Object Browser ▶ Scene Tab ▶ Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Item) ▶ **Deactivate/Activate Sewing (Selected)** → Deactivated Sewing Lines appear in white in the 2D and the 3D window and their names appear in dark grey in the Scene Tab.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for activating or deactivating Sewing Lines in garment design, specifically for adjustments needed after draping, such as adding back slits to men's jackets.

title: Windows - CLO Network Version Installation
content: **Objective** Install Windows - CLO Network Version. Any Asset downloaded in the previous version is maintained when a new version is installed (ver5.0.0.) ** Operation** 1. Run the DVD received upon purchase or the install file received via email. 2. After running the install file, press "Next" on the setup window to continue installation. ![1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026338848/1.png) 3. Review the License Agreement and click "I Agree" to accept the terms of the agreement. ![2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026338868/2.png) 4. Choose a location to install the program. ![3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026338908/3.png) 5. Select a Start Menu folder. ![4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026298687/4.png) 6. The product begins installing. It takes less than a minute. ![5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026338888/5.png) 7. After the installation is completed, click "Finish" to close the window. ![6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026298667/6.png) 8. Once the program has finished installation, a Server must be set up. 9. Click the link below and check to see if the Sentinel Admin Control Center screen shows up, as it does on the picture below: [ ACC Page ](http://localhost:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html)[![accpage.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001356347/accpage.png) ](http://localhost:1947/)If the following screen does not appear, the HASP Driver must be reinstalled: [Manual Sentinel HASP Driver Installation ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000558507-%EC%84%A4%EC%B9%98-%ED%9B%84-%EB%B0%9C%EC%83%9D%ED%95%A0-%EC%88%98-%EC%9E%88%EB%8A%94-%EB%AC%B8%EC%A0%9C-%ED%95%B4%EA%B2%B0-%EB%B0%8F-%EB%B0%A9%EB%B2%95)As shown below, click on the "Configuration" menu on left of the ACC Page. ![configuration.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001336948/configuration.png) 10. Select "Access to Remote License Managers" as below image. ![accesstoremote.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001336928/accesstoremote.png) 11. Check the "Aggressive Search for Remote Licenses" item as shown below. Enter the IP address of the Server PC in the "Specify Search Parameters" item. Click the "Submit" button. 12. If the HASP Key can be seen as shown below after approximately 10 seconds, then the configuration is successful. ![sentinelkey.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001337068/sentinelkey.png) **※ Note:** ** Identifying Server PC's IP Address ** Start (Windows) Button ▶ All Programs ▶ Accessories ▶ Command Prompt ▶ Enter 'ipconfig' or enter 'cmd' in the 'Run' menu ▶ Enter 'ipconfig' Reference site: <http://www.ghacks.net/2011/05/17/network-troubleshooting-basics-the-ipconfig-command/>
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for installing the CLO Network Version of Windows while ensuring that all previously downloaded assets are retained during the upgrade process.

title: Avatar Measure (ver 6.0)
content: **List of Contents** Basic/Surface Circumference Measure Basic/Surface/Linear Measure Height Measure ### **Objective** Measure the circumference, length and height of the Avatar. Two methods are provided. Either based on the protruding part of the avatar or based on the surface of the curvature. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Measurement 3D Toolbar ▶ ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360091740393/mceclip0.png) Click and hold down the Basic Circumference Measure ** Operation** **Basic/Surface Circumference Measure.** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Click the starting point to be measured and click the second point in the desired direction. → A Basic/Surface Circumference measure is displayed. 3. Click once more when it is in the target shape. → A Basic/Surface Circumference measure is created and the length is displayed. **Basic/Surface/Linear Measure** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Click the start point to be measured and double-click the end point. → A Basic/Surface/Linear Tape Measure is created and its length is displayed. → A Linear Measure runs through the Avatar by connecting the start and end points in a straight line. (ver 6.0) **Height Measure** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Click the point to be measured. → A Height Measure that runs vertically from the clicked point to the ground is created and the length is displayed. **※ Note:** * Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to create vertical/horizontal/45˚ tilt. * Use [Attach to Measure](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000426228-Attach-to-Avatar-Tape) tool to attach the pattern outline or Internal Line to the Avatar Measure. **Go back to the List of Contents**
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions for measuring the circumference, length, and height of the Avatar using two methods based on its protruding features or curvature.

title: Shirring (ver5.1.0)
content: ### **Objective** Express shirring realistically by reducing mesh size of the particular area of the Pattern. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LdaeKbFWgZ8 **Location** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005494467/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png) **Edit Pattern ▶** Select a Line**▶** Property Editor**▶** Selected Line**▶ Shirring**** ** **Operation** 1. Click on a Pattern Outline using the ![____3.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360039919454/____3.jpg)**Transform Pattern** tool or ![____2.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360040742833/____2.jpg)**Edit Pattern** tool. 2. Follow the indicated path below: ** **Property Editor ▶ Selected Line ▶**Shirring **** ** 3. Click to toggle on the check box. → Shirring is applied to the selected line and the shirring symbol appears on the 2D Pattern. The result can be checked on the 3D Garment or on the 2D Pattern after switching the [2D Pattern Rendering Style](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360011148874-2D-Window-Display-Icons-ver5-0-0-and-Above-) to Mesh. 4. Adjust the **Interval** and **Height** of the Shirring. **Interval** | Adjust the distance between each mesh. ---|--- **Height** | Adjust the Height of the Shirring. ** ※Note:** Shirring is applied symmetrically when it is applied to Symmetric Patterns.
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide on how to realistically express shirring in your designs by adjusting the mesh size in the CLO 3D pattern editing tool.

title: Sewing Tension
content: **Sewing Tension** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KXPNHZjz29M \- Adjust sewing Tension to improve 3D Garments’ fit. \- Select the ![Toolbar_Common_Sewing_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003396367/Toolbar_Common_Sewing_Edit.png)**Edit Sewing** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Select the Sewing Line which the sewing Tension needs to be adjusted. \- Selected Sewing Line’s properties appear in the Property Editor. * Strength : Type in a value to adjust selected Sewing Line’s Tension Strength. * Ratio : Adjust the Tension Ratio to express how various types of Sewing method influence garment drapes. **※****Note: ** The maximum Tension Ratio is 200%.
content_description: Learn how to adjust sewing tension to enhance the fit of your 3D garments by using the Edit Sewing tool and modifying tension strength and ratio in this informative guide.

title: Slider Gizmo
content: **List of Contents** Move Rotate **Objective** Move or rotate slider to adjust its distance from zipper tape. **Location ** Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Select/Move ** 3D Toolbar ▶**![Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000819148/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) **Select/Move **** ** Operation** **Move** 1. [Create a zipper.](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/115004529388-%EC%A7%80%ED%8D%BC-%EC%83%9D%EC%84%B1) 2. While the Simulation is turned off, follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Select/Move ** 3D Toolbar ▶**![Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000819148/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) Select/Move** 3. Click the slider. → The slider is selected and its **Gizmo** appears. 4. Click and drag the blue segment of the **Gizmo** to move the slider back and forth. Sliders cannot be moved along with Y and Z axes. **Rotate** 1. With the**![Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000819148/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) Select/Move** tool, click on the slider to access the Slider Gizmo. 2. Click and drag the blue circle of the **Gizmo** to rotate on Y axis. Click and drag the yellow-green circle of the **Gizmo** to rotate on X axis. Click and drag the red circle of the **Gizmo** to rotate on Z axis. → The selected zipper slider rotates based on the selected circle. 3. To rotate the puller only, click on the puller while the slider is selected. → The selected puller is highlighted in yellow and the **Gizmo** changes accordingly. 4. Rotate the puller referencing #2. **※ Note:** To reset slider's position and angle, right click on the slider and select [**Reset Slider Arrangement**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-ua/articles/115004681608) option. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for moving and rotating the zipper slider in a 3D garment design tool, enabling precise adjustments to its position and orientation.

title: Edit 3D Pen (Garment)
content: **List of Contents** Select/Move Delete ### **Objective** Edit lines created on 3D Garments. **Location** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Edit_Line__3D_Pattern_.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000022028/Edit_Line__3D_Pattern_.png) **Edit 3D Pen (Garment)** ** Operation** **Select/Move** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Edit_Line__3D_Pattern_.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000022028/Edit_Line__3D_Pattern_.png) **Edit 3D Pen (Garment)** 2. Click the desired segment. → The selected segment is highlighted in yellow and its length appears (ver5.0.0.) 3.
